summary: This htaccess snippet redirects all incoming requests to a maintenance.php page, but only for visitors whose IP addresses aren't on a whitelist. It's a common way to put a website in maintenance mode while allowing specific people (like developers) to access the real site.

explanations.1: IfModule checks if Apache has the rewrite module installed; if not, it skips this entire block.
explanations.2: RewriteEngine On activates Apache's URL rewriting feature, which lets us redirect requests.
explanations.3: RewriteCond is a condition that must be true for the rewrite rule to apply; the ! means 'NOT', so this says 'only continue if the visitor is NOT from 127.0.0.1 (localhost)'.
explanations.4: Same idea as line 3, but checking against the literal string 'localhost'.
explanations.5: Another condition: only continue if the visitor's IP is not the placeholder value 'ADD_YOUR_IP_HERE' (you'd replace this with actual allowed IPs).
explanations.6: This condition says 'only continue if the requested file is NOT maintenance.php', so people accessing maintenance.php directly aren't redirected again (avoiding an infinite loop).
explanations.7: RewriteRule is the actual redirect: take any request (.*) and send it to /maintenance.php; [L,NC,QSA] means 'Last rule, No Case sensitivity, and keep query strings attached'.
